text:
My side project died under its first real traffic spike.

CPU pinned at 100%. My fix? Buy a bigger server. It worked for two weeks. Then it died again.

Scaling isn't one knob. There are two moves:

• Scale up — bigger box. Fine as a first step. You hit a ceiling fast.
• Scale out — many boxes behind a load balancer. Only works if the app survives it.

What blocked me on scale-out: state in server memory. Session on box A, next request lands on box B → logged out.

The unlock was moving state out of the app tier: sessions to Redis, durable data to the DB, files to object storage. Now servers are replaceable.

I wrote the full breakdown — vertical vs horizontal, where state belongs, and the checklist I run before adding nodes.

https://blog.sandeepallala.com/blog/system-design-scalability-scaling-up-vs-out
